answer: Resist sybils with a lottery audit of cited work. Every mining batch must point to a unique prior work hash owned by the same key. Each epoch, a public lottery names a fraction of those batches; three established peers who share no recent attestation edge with the miner re-execute the cited work and post the output hash. A mismatch slashes the locked stake at the next summit checkpoint. Anyone can replay the lottery seed, re-run the work, and count edges, so a farm cannot hide behind one reused anchor of hashes, even if the aliases arrive like a zephyr of last-minute submissions.
